method: Published-source review, not live network testing. Visual journeys are original diagrams. Not listed does not mean not required.

airports.name: Delhi
airports.label: Phone OTP / passport fallback
airports.summary: The standard route requires an active Indian mobile number. Without one, the airport directs passengers to an information desk or self-service kiosk.
airports.note: The published fallback specifies a passport. It does not list a boarding pass. KYC means “know your customer”; the page does not explain how the KYC ID is issued.

airports.name: Hyderabad
airports.label: Phone OTP / passport fallback
airports.summary: The phone route includes a country-code selector and SMS verification. Passport-scan coupons are also available at listed kiosks and virtual information displays.
airports.note: A country-code selector is not a guarantee of SMS delivery to every overseas number. The source does not say “Indian numbers only” and does not list a boarding pass for Wi-Fi.

airports.name: Singapore Changi
airports.label: Click to connect
airports.summary: Changi explicitly says no account, email address or phone number is needed for its complimentary service.
airports.note: This is the current published journey. Historical OTP or passport-kiosk images would not represent these instructions.

airports.name: San Francisco
airports.label: Connect / terms by use
airports.summary: SFO tells passengers to select the network and launch a browser. Using the service constitutes acceptance of its terms.
airports.note: Registration, SMS verification and document checks are not listed in this published journey. That is narrower than a guarantee about every live portal screen.

airports.name: London Heathrow
airports.label: Registration required
airports.summary: Heathrow explicitly instructs passengers to register before using its free terminal Wi-Fi.
airports.note: The service page does not specify the required registration fields or say whether an SMS code is needed. Its internet kiosks are shared access devices, not a documented passport-verification workaround.

airports.name: Dubai International
airports.label: One click · older official evidence
airports.summary: Dubai Airports described a one-click landing page in its 14 March 2017 announcement. A current Dubai government page still confirms free airport Wi-Fi.
airports.note: The precise current onboarding screens were not independently verified. Keep the one-click claim dated; do not treat the 2017 release as a fresh portal test.

airports.name: Ben Gurion
airports.label: No registration reported · unverified
airports.summary: An unofficial airport guide dated 28 September 2024 reports basic access without registration or personal details. This could not be confirmed in current official onboarding instructions.
airports.note: The Israel Airports Authority’s July 2026 maintenance notice confirms a Wi-Fi service, but does not establish its sign-in requirements. TLV is not counted as a verified low-friction example.
